key_insight: ROS-LLM is an open-source ROS framework that lets non-experts command and teach robots using natural language, demonstrations, and feedback, while automatically tuning actions to make performance reliable in real-world tasks.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between large language models and embodied robots by lowering the expertise needed to program robots, enabling learning from human demonstrations/feedback, and improving robustness and sim-to-real reliability for practical deployment.
method: Embed LLMs as high-level planners within a ROS-native architecture to convert natural language into grounded robot actions and plans.
Enable skill acquisition via learning-from-demonstration plus human feedback loops so robots can be taught new tasks by non-experts.
Automatic action-parameter tuning and runtime monitoring to adapt policies for consistent, reliable real-world execution.
impact: Lowers the barrier to robot programming and speeds prototyping of embodied AI systems; provides a reproducible, open-source platform for integrating LLMs into robotics research and real-world applications.
visual_elements: System architecture diagram: ROS nodes + LLM node, perception, planner, actuator modules and data flows.
Loop diagram: Natural language → LLM planning → execution → sensor feedback → human corrective feedback → model/parameter update.
Before/after reliability chart: task success rate and variance without vs. with auto-tuning and feedback.
Storyboard/demo panel: non-expert issuing a voice/text command and then teaching a new skill via demonstration.
paper_title: A robot operating system framework for using large language models in embodied AI
paper_authors: Christopher E. Mower, Yuhui Wan, Hongzhan Yu, Antoine Grosnit, Jonas Gonzalez-Billandon
